system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}

CONCEPT: Weak acyclicity
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: The dependency graph with universal and existential edges, and the "no cycle through an existential edge" condition. Covers the polynomial bound on standard-chase length, its relation to rich acyclicity and safety, and its incomparability with oblivious-chase termination.

ATOMS:
- CS-DB-C02-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: A set Σ of tgds is weakly acyclic if its dependency graph has no cycle going through an existential edge.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0026-s21] ▶Deﬁnition 34. [19] A set of tgds Σ is said to be weakly acyclic if the corresponding dependency graph does not have any cycle going through an existential edge.
- CS-DB-C02-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: For a set of tgds Σ over a schema, the dependency graph has the schema's positions as vertices. It has an edge from position (R,i) to position (S,j) when some tgd α(x̄,ȳ) → ∃z̄ β(x̄,z̄) in Σ has a universally quantified variable x ∈ x̄ at (R,i) in α, and either x also occurs at (S,j) in β (a universal edge) or an existential variable z ∈ z̄ occurs at (S,j) in β (an existential edge).
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0026-s16] The dependency graph associated with Σ is a directed edge-labeled graph GΣ = (V, E), such that the set of vertexes V represents the positions in R.
    [CS-DB-p0026-s17] There is an edge ((R, i), (S, j)) ∈E, if there exists a dependency ξ ∈Σ of the form α(¯x, ¯y) →∃¯z β(¯x, ¯z).
    [CS-DB-p0026-s18] There exists x ∈¯x such that x occurs in position (R, i) in α and if one of the following holds: 1. x occurs in β in position (S, j).
    [CS-DB-p0026-s19] In this case the edge is labeled as universal; 2. there exists variable z ∈¯z which occurs in position (S, j) in β.
    [CS-DB-p0026-s20] In this case the edge is labeled as existential.
- CS-DB-C02-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: Weak acyclicity intuitively checks that the set of tgds has no cyclic condition in which one new null value forces the addition of another new null value.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0026-s14] Intuitively weak acyclicity checks if the set of tgds does not have a cyclic condition such that another new null value forces the adding of a new null value.
- CS-DB-C02-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: If Σ is a weakly acyclic set of tgds and I is an instance, there is a polynomial in the size of I that bounds the length of every standard-chase sequence of I and Σ.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0026-s28] ▶Theorem 35. [19] Let Σ ∈WA and let I be an instance.
    [CS-DB-p0026-s29] Then there exists a polynomial in size of I that bounds the length of every standard-chase sequence of I and Σ.
- CS-DB-C02-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: Testing whether a set Σ of tgds is weakly acyclic can be done in time polynomial in the size of Σ.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0026-s23] Note that the problem of testing if Σ ∈WA is polynomial in size of Σ.
- CS-DB-C02-S2-03.r1 | S2
  ATOM: The class WA of weakly acyclic tgd sets is closed under semi-enrichment.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0027-s04] From the observation that the class WA is closed under semi-enrichment, Theorem 35 and Corollary 27, it follows:
- CS-DB-C02-S3-01.r1a | S3
  ATOM: The class RA of richly acyclic tgd sets is contained in the class WA of weakly acyclic tgd sets ($RA \subseteq WA$), which follows from the definitions of the two classes.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0026-s26] From the deﬁnitions of the RA and WA classes, it follows that RA ⊆WA.
- CS-DB-C02-S3-01.r1b | S3
  ATOM: The inclusion of the class RA of richly acyclic tgd sets in the class WA of weakly acyclic tgd sets is strict ($RA \subset WA$), because there is a tgd set $\Sigma_2$ that is weakly acyclic but not richly acyclic.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0026-s27] Also because Σ2 ∈WA and Σ2 /∈RA, it follows that the inclusion is strict, that is RA ⊂WA.
- CS-DB-C02-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: S3, rank 3: The class of weakly acyclic tgd sets is strictly contained in the class of safe tgd sets.
  EVIDENCE:
    [CS-DB-p0028-s15] From our running example in this subsection and from the deﬁnition of the SD class, it follows that WA ⊂SD.
